title: AES-128 Optical fault experiment on 8-bit smartcard (Giraud, AES2004 proceedings published 2005)

target.description: Full AES-128 master-key recovery in the described optical-injection experiment on an 8-bit smartcard with known implementation code; no chip model is specified.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Keys of the stated AES implementation without a weak-key restriction; fault protections are outside the model.
setting.plaintext_model: Repeat encryptions of the same plaintext under the same key; retain its correct ciphertext as a reference. Counts of faulty ciphertexts exclude that reusable reference unless explicitly stated otherwise.

fault_model.target: AES state and online expanded-key operations on the tested 8-bit smartcard, attacked with a microscope and modified camera flash.
fault_model.granularity: Useful single-byte faults selected from a physical process that often disturbed four or eight bytes.
fault_model.timing: Flash synchronized to the intermediate operations needed by the second attack; exact measured per-stage physical timing windows are not supplied.
fault_model.location: The experiment first located sensitive chip areas and synchronized the flash; many induced errors failed the useful-byte model.
fault_model.value_control: Optical disturbance with no chosen fault difference; multi-byte outputs require rejection.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Every faulty output is matched to the same fixed-input correct reference; useful faults, random-location ciphertexts and physical executions have distinct accounting.

assumptions: A round key is used correctly for encryption and then faulted before generating the next round key. The implementation expands keys on the fly.
The reported outcome and data budget use the paper's candidate-filtering model; no numerical whole-key success rate is inferred from a byte-level statistic.
The attacker uses known AES implementation code on an 8-bit smartcard. Apparatus cost, calibration effort and chip-to-chip variability are not quantified.

time.note: No numerical whole-endpoint runtime is reported for this version and endpoint.

data.note: Observed execution count needed in the described physical experiment, including attempts yielding unsuitable faults. It is neither a useful-fault count nor a universal lower bound on AES attack cost.

memory.note: The article describes counters or candidate lists without a numerical peak-memory budget.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing-time budget is reported. The Appendix A 8×2^8 equation tests per useful output are a component count, not a complete attack cost.

success.description: No numerical whole-output recovery probability is supplied for this exact endpoint and sample budget. The smartcard demonstration required more than1000 AES executions, including many unusable multi-byte disturbances. One successful demonstration has no repeated-trial denominator and does not measure whole-key success or useful-fault yield.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Theoretical deterministic guarantees require the stated ideal model; local filters, characteristic products, expected counts and physical acquisition are separate. Costs, targets, settings, existing conflicts and full-audit gates are unchanged.

components.description: Sections4.1–4.3: with effective faults at the modeled windows and correct earlier-stage material, the actual subkey/state satisfies the complete candidate equations. This is conditional candidate inclusion, not unique recovery or physical acquisition success.

evidence.interpretation: Version-specific endpoint retaining its target, prior information, fault controls and native sample accounting.

evidence.locator: Complete proceedingsPDF1–15/printed27–41 and earlyPS15-page reading rendition; Sections3–6, AppendixA and references.
evidence.interpretation: Full exact-edition text and AES contribution inventory reviewed; component checks and whole-attack reproduction are separate.

evidence.locator: Proceedings PDF12–13 / printed38–39 Section6; construction PDF7–12 Sections4.1–4.3.

The smartcard demonstration required more than1000 AES executions, including many unusable multi-byte disturbances. One successful demonstration has no repeated-trial denominator and does not measure whole-key success or useful-fault yield.

limitations: Useful faulty ciphertext counts do not automatically include ineffective physical injections or calibration attempts.
The article does not supply a measured success frequency, runtime or peak memory for every target and parameter choice.
